idiom_name: @dynamicMemberLookup + subscript(dynamicMember:) over a [String: Any] or JSON store
implementation_notes: SE-0195 gives Swift user-defined dynamic member lookup: on a @dynamicMemberLookup type member lookup always succeeds, falling back to subscript(dynamicMember:) with the member name, while declared members still win; the subscript may return an Optional or a typed JSON wrapper so absence stays visible. The property list is your dictionary (or a JSON enum such as the proposal's), and SE-0252 adds a key-path overload for statically typed member access. The classic owner/descriptor structure is replaced - no wrapper classes are needed - but the compiler cannot check the names either.
pitfalls: Typo'd members compile: lookup always succeeds, so order.colour yields nil (or an empty wrapper) instead of a diagnostic - validate names explicitly and keep a strict accessor API where correctness matters.
[String: Any] is not Codable, so dynamic JSON needs JSONSerialization, a hand-written Decodable wrapper or the proposal's JSON enum, and Any erases the value's static type until it is cast.

@dynamicMemberLookup may only be written on the primary type declaration, not on an extension, and mixing the string overload with the SE-0252 KeyPath overload changes which members resolve first (declared members and key paths take priority).
